On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6 to 70.0 under standard conditions and from 33.3 to 53.3 under OOD perturbations, surpassing the baseline in both settings. @ l@ l@ Correspondence: & \\ Project Page: & kingzein.github.io/weave-vla -1 Introduction sec:intro Vision-language-action (VLA) models combine pretrained vision-language representations with robot demonstrations to learn instruction-conditioned manipulation policies. Representative approaches such as OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT have advanced general-purpose manipulation, while recent systems have expanded these capabilities across robotic embodiments~ kim2024openvla,kim2025fine,nvidia2026gr00tn17 . Flow-based policies, including , , and , further advance continuous action generation, generalization, and steerable control~ black2024pi0,intelligence2025pi_,intelligence2026pi07steerablegeneralistrobotic . Despite these advances, understanding and maintaining the spatial relationships that govern manipulation remains an important challenge. Robot actions depend on different relative 3D relations at different stages of manipulation. For example, placing a cup into a bowl requires reasoning about gripper--cup relations during grasping and cup--bowl relations during placement, while other object pairs may be less relevant. These relations change with robot and object motion, while geometric estimation errors, viewpoint changes, and occasional occlusion can make their current configurations difficult to determine reliably~ peng2026spatialbench . SpatialVLA and 3DS-VLA improve spatial awareness through geometric representations and sequential spatial constraints~ qu2025spatialvla,li2025threedsvla . GraphCoT-VLA and TriRelVLA further explore structured 3D relations for manipulation~ huang2026graphcotvla, zhou2026trirelvla . This raises a central question: How can VLA models explicitly model task-relevant 3D relations and continuously update their representations as manipulation unfolds to support action generation? To address this challenge, we introduce WeaveVLA, a framework that explicitly models task-relevant relative 3D relations and their evolution during manipulation to enhance VLA action generation, as illustrated in Fig.~ fig:teaser . Its object-centric representation combines visual features with estimated 3D geometry, using the robot's tool center point (TCP) to anchor gripper--object relations. A task-conditioned graph connects instruction-relevant objects, the gripper, and nearby spatial references, while edge-aware graph attention encodes their relative 3D geometry. To maintain evolving spatial context, WeaveVLA assigns a recurrent state to each selected entity pair and updates it with valid geometric evidence across observations. The resulting relation features are conditioned on the vision-language context and summarized into compact relational tokens. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages the learned relational features to preserve spatial structure. Together with the original vision-language representations, these tokens condition a continuous action expert for robot manipulation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on two VLA backbones, StarVLA-GR00T and , and evaluate its effectiveness on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN~ mees2022calvin . On the four standard LIBERO suites, WeaveVLA achieves average success rates of 98.3 and 98.2 , respectively, improving both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, it improves StarVLA-GR00T from 74.9 to 82.0 and from 85.7 to 87.8 , demonstrating consistent gains across the two architectures. On CALVIN D D, WeaveVLA increases the average completed sequence length from 3.645 to 3.910 for StarVLA-GR00T, surpassing the original baseline, and from 3.885 to 3.997 for . Across three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based WeaveVLA achieves average success rates of 70.0 under standard conditions and 53.3 under perturbations, outperforming both baselines. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: We introduce WeaveVLA, a 3D relational grounding framework that explicitly models task-relevant spatial relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references to enhance VLA action generation. We develop pair-specific recurrent relational updating to maintain evolving 3D relations across observations, integrating valid geometric evidence while preserving historical relational context. We demonstrate consistent improvements across two VLA backbones on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN D D, and validate WeaveVLA on three real-world manipulation tasks, outperforming both baselines under standard and OOD conditions. Related Work sec:related Vision-Language-Action Models Building on pretrained vision-language representations and robot demonstrations, vision-language-action (VLA) research has advanced toward more generalizable robot manipulation. Early approaches such as RT-2 and OpenVLA demonstrated the transfer of visual-semantic knowledge to robotic control~ brohan2023rt2,kim2024openvla . OpenVLA-OFT improved action generation efficiency through continuous action representations, parallel decoding, and action chunking~ kim2025fine . Subsequent VLA architectures further advanced continuous action generation and manipulation across diverse tasks~ black2024pi0,gr00t2025,pan2026worldtowrist . More recent models have expanded generalization and adaptability, with demonstrating generalization to unseen environments~ intelligence2025pi_ and advancing steerable execution and compositional generalization~ intelligence2026pi07steerablegeneralistrobotic . LingBot-VLA 2.0 and GR00T N1.7 further advanced cross-embodiment manipulation~ wu2026lingbotvla2,nvidia2026gr00tn17 , while Gemini Robotics 2 extended generalist control to whole-body and dexterous manipulation. WeaveVLA complements these advances by augmenting VLA action generation with explicit, task-relevant 3D spatial relations. Spatial Grounding for Robotic Manipulation Spatial grounding connects visual observations with the geometric structure of the environment to support robotic manipulation. Recent studies have incorporated explicit 3D representations into VLA policies. SpatialVLA introduces 3D positional encoding to enhance spatial awareness~ qu2025spatialvla , while 3DS-VLA combines 2D-3D feature alignment with sequential spatial constraints for manipulation~ li2025threedsvla . Graph-based representations have also been explored for spatial relation modeling in navigation and autonomous driving, exemplified by BSG and GraphAD~ liu2023bsg,zhang2024graphad . Graph-of-Mark further enhances spatial reasoning for multimodal models via graph-based visual prompting~ gom2026aaai . For robotic manipulation, scene graphs have been used for both high-level planning and action conditioning. Compose by Focus employs task-relevant graphs to condition diffusion-based manipulation skills~ qi2026focus , while GraSP-VLA uses scene graphs for symbolic planning and policy orchestration~ neau2025graspvla . SIR further learns task-relevant graph sparsification for action generation~ mattes2026sir . More directly, GraphCoT-VLA combines an updatable 3D pose-object graph with structured reasoning~ huang2026graphcotvla , while TriRelVLA models object-hand-task relations to condition action prediction~ zhou2026trirelvla . Other studies have explored spatiotemporal representations for manipulation: ConsisVLA-4D addresses spatiotemporal consistency~ li2026consisvla , semantic-geometric task representations jointly encode object relations and motion histories~ herbert2026semantic , and Qian et al. maintain dynamic scene graphs as structured memory under partial observability~ qian2026scenegraphs . While these studies demonstrate the value of spatial structure and temporal context, WeaveVLA focuses on explicitly encoding task-relevant relative 3D relations for action generation. A task-conditioned graph captures gripper--object and object--reference geometry, while observation-aware recurrent updates maintain pair-specific relational states across observations. Method sec:method WeaveVLA grounds robot actions in task-relevant relative 3D relations, as illustrated in Fig.~ fig:overview . Given RGB observations from the available cameras, proprioception , and instruction , the framework associates tracked entities with visual features and estimated 3D geometry. A task-conditioned graph organizes relative spatial relations among relevant objects, the gripper, and nearby references, while pair-specific recurrent states maintain these relations across observations. A learned-query readout then extracts compact relational tokens from the updated graph features, which complement the original vision-language context to condition a continuous action expert. Object-Centric Observation Representation sec:perception To ground 3D spatial relations, WeaveVLA first establishes object-centric visual representations with consistent identities across observations. At episode initialization, an adapted YOLOE detector~ wang2025yoloe supplies labeled boxes to frozen SAM~3~ carion2025sam3 ; Cutie~ cheng2024cutie then propagates instance masks and identities. Robot regions are excluded from object instance masks before feature pooling. Object appearance features are pooled from visual tokens aligned with instance masks in the same camera view, while the original VLM retains its backbone-specific camera inputs. Since visual tokens may only partially overlap an object, we aggregate instance features according to their foreground coverage. Its finger masks are obtained from robot geometry and camera calibration, and appearance features are pooled from visible finger regions using the same foreground-coverage weighting.
